title: Comet mining in Leaving Sol
author: pottrell
selftext:
Busters away! Mining drones, go! Slowly building out skills in my Leaving Sol space game! Level 55 Mining introduces comet mining for valuable resources used in the engineering skill. Can you maintain a stable run? 

https://leavingsol.com

Built in Unity 6, but all the actual game logic lives in a separate C# library. This means the future multiplayer server and the phone will run exactly the same rules. There's around 540 automated tests and a simulation that runs weeks of in-game economic activity to check things don't fall apart.

The galaxy contains around 100 million star systems, generated deterministically so every player sees exactly the same universe. Sol's real stellar neighbours are positioned accurately. I would note, as the game progresses, more of the generated systems will be tweaked/built on.

Newtonian flight, Keplerian planetary orbits, fixed-step physics and double precision.

Ships and stations are modelled in Blender using Python scripts. Even the sound effects are generated programmatically using Python.

It started life as a browser prototype before I moved everything into Unity.

I've made extensive use of Claude Code along the way. I'm a developer during the day, so AI has been a huge help getting something of this scope off the ground. The ideas, design decisions and direction are mine, albeit inspired by what I've also seen, with AI assisting heavily with implementation. Because of the development approach, it's meant I've been able to play with Blender/Unity with some nice base models to learn the software instead of starting from scratch.

Music in this clip is by Hans Zimmer of course
